title: The Blind Men and the Elephant
text:
Some monks came to the Buddha after their alms round in Savatthi. They had seen teachers of rival sects arguing in the town, each insisting that his own view was the only truth and wounding the others with sharp words. The Buddha answered with a story.

Long ago, he said, a king of that same city ordered all the men born blind to be gathered together. Then he had an elephant brought before them. One blind man was led to touch its head, another its ear, others the tusk, the trunk, the body, a leg, the back, the tail and the tuft at the end of the tail.

Then the king asked each of them what an elephant was like. The one who had felt the head said it was like a water pot. The one who had touched the ear said a winnowing basket. The tusk was a plowshare, the trunk a plow pole, the body a storeroom, the leg a pillar, the back a mortar, the tail a pestle, the tuft a broom.

Each was sure he was right. They began to shout, "An elephant is like this!" "No, it is not!" until they were hitting each other with their fists, while the king looked on and laughed.
lesson: Your experience of a problem is real but partial. Before arguing, ask what the other person has touched that you have not.
people: The Buddha, a king, blind men
